subject: general
question: Which ministry launched a special campaign namely Kanya Shiksha Pravesh Utsav launched on 7th March, 2022 to re-enroll out of school adolescent girls (OoS AG) in the age group of 11-14 years?

options.text: Ministry of Women and Child Development
Ministry of Health and family Welfare

solution:
The correct answer is __**Ministry of Women and Child Development**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The **Kanya Shiksha Pravesh Utsav** campaign was launched by the Ministry of Women and Child Development on **7th March 2022**.
 
• This campaign aims to re-enroll out-of-school adolescent girls (OoS AG) in the age group of **11-14 years**.
 
• The initiative is in collaboration with the **Ministry of Education** and **UNICEF**.
 
• The campaign focuses on fulfilling the right to education and ensuring that girls continue their education by addressing drop-out rates.
 
• Efforts under this campaign include community mobilization, tracking, and monitoring of out-of-school adolescent girls to bring them back to the educational fold.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **UNICEF**

 
 
• UNICEF, or the United Nations Children's Fund, is a UN agency responsible for providing humanitarian and developmental aid to children worldwide.
 
• It is one of the most widely recognized and well-known social welfare organizations in the world.
 
• UNICEF’s programs focus on child health and nutrition, safe water and sanitation, quality basic education, and the protection of children from violence, exploitation, and AIDS.
 
• It works in over 190 countries and territories to save children's lives, to defend their rights, and to help them fulfill their potential.
 
 
 
• **Right to Education (RTE) Act, 2009**
 
 
• The Right to Education Act, also known as the RTE Act, was enacted by the Parliament of India on 4 August 2009.
 
• It mandates free and compulsory education for children between the ages of 6 and 14 years under Article 21A of the Indian Constitution.
 
• The Act lays down norms and standards relating to Pupil-Teacher Ratios (PTRs), buildings and infrastructure, school-working days, and teacher-working hours.
 
• It also provides for the prohibition of unrecognized schools from practice, and the prohibition of private tuition by teachers.
 
 
 
• **Ministry of Women and Child Development (MWCD)**
 
 
• The Ministry of Women and Child Development is a branch of the Government of India.
 
• It was established with the mandate to formulate and administer the rules and regulations and laws relating to women and child development in India.
 
• The primary areas of concern for the Ministry include the welfare and development of women and children.
 
• It is responsible for implementing various social welfare schemes and programs aimed at improving the lives of women and children in India.
 
 
 
• **Ministry of Education**
 
 
• The Ministry of Education is responsible for the formulation, implementation, and monitoring of education policies in India.
 
• It oversees various educational levels ranging from primary and secondary to higher education.
 
• The Ministry works to ensure that educational institutions maintain standards and provide quality education to all students.
 
• It also collaborates with other ministries and international bodies to promote educational development in the country.
